jobs.description: Job available in 4 locations: Berlin, Halle, Remote, LeipzigWork ScheduleStandard (Mon-Fri)Environmental ConditionsOfficeJob DescriptionJob DescriptionAs part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.The Clinical Diagnostics Division (CDD) provides innovative diagnostic solutions across selected in vitro diagnostics (IVD) market segments and has been a trusted partner to the IVD industry for more than 40 years.Our portfolio includes solutions for drugs-of-abuse testing, therapeutic drug monitoring, quality control, sepsis diagnosis, prenatal screening and more. In addition, CDD offers advanced laboratory instrumentation and high-throughput automation solutions for a wide range of clinical laboratory environments.Our products and solutions are delivered through direct sales, regional distributors and OEM partnerships.Location:Field-based / Remote within the territory - Eastern/ Central GermanyIdeally based in e.g. Halle, Leipzig or BerlinDiscover Impactful WorkJoin our Clinical Customer Development team as a Clinical Customer Development Specialist and support the targeted clinical use of Procalcitonin (PCT) and other innovative biomarkers.In this field-based role, you will lead clinical market development across your territory and increase awareness, acceptance and sustainable adoption of our biomarkers through targeted engagement with healthcare professionals, clinical education and development activities. In doing so, you will support the diagnosis and management of bacterial infections and sepsis, as well as antimicrobial stewardship initiatives, and contribute to advancing biomarker-guided clinical decision-making.You will take ownership of clinical market development within your territory, with the goal of increasing demand, acceptance and sustainable clinical adoption of our biomarkers. The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Every year, 225.000 patients are treated in 30 clinics, 27 institutes and specialized centers. The over 8.000 employees offer medical care with state-of-the-art diagnosis and therapies, which meet highest international standards. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral antivity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.At the Insitute of Medical Microbiology (working group of PD Dr. Torben Knuschke), we are therefore offering the following position, which is fully funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and will start on 1 January 2027Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) funtions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cellsApply molecular biology techniquesPlan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studiesPresent research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publicationsAssist in supervising Bachelors/Masters studentsA completed Master´s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related fieldSolid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniquesExperience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantageStrong interest in basic research in Virology/ImmunologyIndependent, structured, and team-oriented working-styleExcellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredAn exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research fieldDedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminarsState-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital EssenInterdisciplinary work with colleagues from other departmentsEnrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Sciences BIOME (https://www.uni-due.de/biome)Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 yearsA collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideasFamily-friendly corporate culture

GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. They will synthesize these results to deliver the first global ULVZ map based on dynamic simulations and to discriminate among proposed ULVZ compositions. The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that links basic and clinical sciences to improve prevention, diagnosis and therapy of Diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Junior Research Group Crosstalk (head: Dr. Melanie Mittenbühler) at the Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry focuses on how inter-tissue communication impacts energy balance and metabolic health. We are seeking a talented and highly motivatedPostdoctoral Fellow (PhD/Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 100%) to join our research group. Our group investigates how skeletal muscle acts as an endocrine organ and communicates with other tissues through secreted signaling molecules, particularly myokines. In the ERC Starting Grant project MYOSCAN, we systematically investigate how exercise and age-related muscle loss alter the skeletal muscle secretome. We aim to identify novel exercise-sensitive myokines and define their roles in sarcopenia, metabolic disease, and cancer biology. A central question is whether muscle-derived factors promote or suppress tumor growth and how these signaling pathways can be therapeutically targeted.PhD in molecular biology, cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, exercise science, metabolism, cancer biology, or a related fieldStrong expertise in at least one of the following areas: proteomics/mass spectrometry, secretome analysis, cell biology, molecular signaling, metabolic research, or cancer biology. You will be able to learn state-of-the-art methodologies in a team of young scientists. Initially, the position is to be awarded for 2 years starting from 01.03.2027 or later. An extension of the contract period is envisaged. The employment contract is governed by TV-L in its current version for North Rhine-Westphalia, including the special regulations regarding the scientific area. The salary is based on qualification and experience, according to TV-L.Females are especially encouraged to apply, and in the case of equal qualification, handicapped persons will be given preference. The German Diabetes Center is committed to family-friendly working conditions and equal gender policy. Since May 2011, the DDZ is a “Career and Family” audit-acknowledged center.
